content: Characterization testing (Feathers, corroborated across multiple sources): the technique records observed current behaviour, never intended behaviour. Procedure: call the unit with a specific input, assert a value you know is wrong, run it, read the real value from the failure output, paste that in, rename the test to describe the behaviour, repeat. Every expected value must come from observed execution - values derived from docs, comments, or intent are guesses. Strong guidance for this phase: (1) do not freeze implementation details - prefer externally meaningful behaviour (state transitions, queue payloads, retry behaviour, idempotency, critical error handling) over internal structure; (2) when a characterization test reveals a bug, keep the test green against current behaviour, mark it suspicious with a marker comment, and fix in a separate change - never change the assertion and the implementation in the same commit, or a red build stops telling you which happened; (3) a suite that never fails when the code is deliberately broken provides no safety net (mutation check); (4) capture side effects (writes, ordering, counts), not only return values.
